title: Sensor step controls removed the central Arctic ice area link from September to March in 1979-2023
abstract: We tested regional sea ice memory with Sea Ice Index Version 4. A scan of 14 northern regions found a strong central Arctic ice area link between September 1979-2023 and March 1980-2024 after linear trend removal. Controls for two documented sensor transitions reduced the correlation from 0.810 to -0.040 and the slope from 0.693 to -0.009. The step-controlled slope had a conditional 95% three-year block interval of -0.087 to 0.091. Within 1988-2006 and 2008-2023, the correlations were 0.014 and -0.052. Adding the documented missing polar area at assumed ice concentrations of 80-100% reduced the correlation to 0.342-0.128. These checks show that the original link is sensitive to known coverage changes. They do not produce a corrected climate record or establish that physical memory is absent. The central result was selected after the regional scan. Small samples, changing climate, missing polar concentration, and aggregate data limit inference. Code, fixed monthly evidence, provenance, regional tables, a figure and checks are supplied.

display.caption: Linear trend removal leaves a strong seasonal link. Separate controls for documented sensor transitions remove this link in the tested central Arctic area record. Credit: Sea Ice Index, National Snow and Ice Data Center.
